A ScheduleTable shall have at least one expiry point.
An expiry point shall contain a (possibly empty) set of Tasks to activate.
An expiry point shall contain a (possibly empty) set of Events to set.
An expiry point shall contain an offset in ticks from the start of the ScheduleTable .
An expiry point shall activate at least one Task OR set at least one event OR replenish a Tasks execution budget.
The delay between adjacent expiry points shall be in the range OsCounterMinCycle .. OsCounterMaxAllowedValue of the underlying Counter .
A ScheduleTable of the Operating System module shall be driven by exactly one Counter .
The Operating System module shall be able to process at least one ScheduleTable per Counter at any given time.
The Operating System module shall make use of ticks so that one tick on the Counter corresponds to one tick on the ScheduleTable .

If an expiry point contains actions to activate a Task and to set one or several Event (s) of the same Task , then the Operating System module shall process this Task activation before the related Event (s) are set. No further assumptions about the order for the processing of expiry points can be made.
The ScheduleTable shall be configurable as either single-shot or repeating.

When a ScheduleTable switch is requested, the OS shall continue to process expiry points on the current ScheduleTable . After the Final Expiry Point there will be a delay equivalent to Final Delay ticks before processing the switched-to ScheduleTable . The initial expiry point will be processed after initial offset.
An expiry point shall permit the configuration of an OsScheduleTableMaxShorten that defines the maximum number of ticks that can be subtracted from expiry point offset.
An expiry point shall permit the configuration of an OsScheduleTableMaxLengthen that defines the maximum number of ticks that can be added to expiry point offset.

The Operating System module shall start to synchronize an explicitly synchronized ScheduleTable after a synchronization count is provided AND shall continue to adjust expiry points until synchronized.

The Operating System module shall set the state of an explicitly synchronized ScheduleTable to "running and synchronous" if the deviation is less than or equal to the configured OsScheduleTblExplicitPrecision threshold.
The Operating System module shall set the state of an explicitly synchronized ScheduleTable to "running" if the deviation is greater than the configured OsScheduleTblExplicitPrecision threshold.

If in a call of CheckObjectAccess the object to be examined is not a valid object OR <ApplID> is invalid OR <ObjectType> is invalid THEN CheckObjectAccess shall return NO_ACCESS .
The first call to StartOS (for starting the Operating System) shall not return.
If ShutdownOS is called and ShutdownHook returns then the Operating System module shall disable all interrupts and enter an endless loop.
If the ScheduleTable is single-shot, the Operating System module shall allow a Final Delay between 0 .. OsCounterMaxAllowedValue of the underlying Counter .

If ScheduleTable processing has been cancelled before reaching the Final Expiry Point and is subsequently restarted then [SWS_Os_00358]/[SWS_Os_00347] means that the re-start occurs from the start of the ScheduleTable .
A ScheduleTable of the Operating System module that is implicitly synchronized shall have a Duration equal to OsCounterMaxAllowedValue + 1 of its associated OSEK OS Counter .
The Operating System module shall prevent a ScheduleTable that is implicitly synchronized from being started at a relative count value.
A ScheduleTable that is explicitly synchronized shall have a duration no greater than modulus of the drive Counter .

If an explicitly synchronized ScheduleTable was started synchronously, then the Operating System module shall guarantee that it has state "waiting" when the call of service StartScheduleTableSynchron returns.
The value of (Offset - OsScheduleTableMaxShorten ) of an expiry point shall be greater than (Offset + OsCounterMinCycle ) of the pervious expiry point.
The value of ( OsScheduleTableMaxLengthen + delay_from_previous_EP) of an expiry point shall be less than the OsCounterMaxAllowedValue of the underlying Counter .
A ScheduleTable shall define a precision bound with a value in the range 0 to duration.

The Operating System module shall provide the OSEK error macros ( OSError...() ) to all configured error hooks AND there shall be two (like in OIL) global configuration parameters to switch these macros on or off.

If a ScheduleTable has OsScheduleTblSyncStrategy = IMPLICIT and the OsCounterMaxAllowedValue +1 of the associated Counter is not equal to the duration of the ScheduleTable then the consitency check shall issue an error.
Each expiry point on a given ScheduleTable shall have a unique offset.
The Initial Offset shall be zero OR in the range OsCounterMinCycle .. OsCounterMaxAllowedValue of the underlying Counter .
For periodic ScheduleTables the value of Final Delay shall be in the range OsCounterMinCycle .. OsCounterMaxAllowedValue of the underlying Counter .

The Operating System module shall support OS-Applications which are a configurable selection of Trusted Functions, Tasks, ISRs, Alarms, ScheduleTables, Counters, hooks (for startup, error and shutdown).
The Operating System module shall support the notion of trusted and non-trusted OS-Applications.

If the Operating System module terminates an OS-Application, then it shall: • terminate all running, ready and waiting Tasks/ ISRs of the OS-Application AND • disable all interrupts of the OS-Application AND • stop all active alarms of the OS-Applications AND • stop all ScheduleTables of the OS-Application.

The Operating System module shall prevent access of OS-Applications, trusted or non-trusted, to objects not belonging to this OS-Application, except access rights for such objects are explicitly granted by configuration.
CheckTaskMemoryAccess and CheckISRMemoryAccess check the memory access. Memory access checking is possible for all OS-Applications and from all OS-Applications and does not need granted rights.
CheckObjectAccess checks the access rights for Operating System objects. Checking object access is possible for all OS-Applications and from all OS-Applications and does not need granted rights.
The Operating System module shall allow exporting services from trusted OS-Applications.
If the ScheduleTable <ScheduleTableID> in a call of StartScheduleTableRel is implicitely synchronized ( OsScheduleTblSyncStrategy = IMPLICIT), StartScheduleTableRel shall return E_OS_ID .
